open_questions: Centroid is inconclusive (diff_snr 2.848 not used) and centroid_all not run; ground-based follow-up would confirm on-target location and rule out faint blend at arcsec scale.
Planet radius ~3 Rearth is Neptune-sized; RV mass measurement would rule out brown-dwarf / very-eccentric stellar companion otherwise consistent with flat, no-secondary transit.
dossier.public_summary: A 2.5-hour flat-bottom dip recurs every 14.7 days on a nearby 0.27 solar-radius M dwarf with steady depth and no odd-even, secondary or blend warning. The inferred 3 Earth-radius size and lack of stellar eclipses make a Neptune-size planet the best explanation, with mass to be confirmed by Doppler follow-up.

reasons.why: Transit is flat-bottomed, not V-shaped, favoring a planet over a grazing/binary eclipse.
Planet size is well below stars/giant-planet limit, no sign of stellar eclipses.
No odd/even difference (0.3935 sigma) against a binary at twice the period (29.4 d).
No significant secondary (snr 3.543 below 5, best_brightening_snr 2.551), hot-giant secondary ruled out.
Depth steady across 3 sectors (9667, 9742, 9063 ppm chi2 0.09533) and transit_depths p_consistent 0.5324 with 4 transits.
No star within one TESS pixel can cause dip, closest needs 30%+ eclipse at 69.9 arcsec.
Duration within 1.5x central (1.932h) matches M-dwarf host; Gaia radii give 1.19-1.29 ratio and 3.18-3.27 Rearth, still planetary.
Low rank is noted but outweighed by specific evidence above (flat bottom, tiny size, no aliasing/blend) which scorer under-weights, so disagreed with rank.
